newsitem.title: FINLAND: Trendless Helsinki ends lower with overseas.
newsitem.headline: Trendless Helsinki ends lower with overseas.

text.p: Shares slipped in trendless trade on Tuesday, taking their cue from Wall Street's early fall on uncertainty ahead of news from the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy due after the Finnish markets close.
The general HEX index fell 1.22 percent to close at 2,382.4 points and bourse bellwether Nokia closed at at 246.00, down 8.50 markka or 3.3 percent, reflecting Wall Street's volatility.
"All this volatility is putting people off," one broker said. Strong November U.S. housing starts data knocked bonds in the afternoon and spread woes around the stock market as well.

The outlook depended on what the U.S. central bankers decide and brokers said there were expectations that they would not move rates amid signs that the U.S. economy is settling down as the year draws to a close. But sentiment was nervous.
Finland's third largest forest industry group Metsa-Serla fell 0.70 markka or two percent to close at 32.00 markka on its acquisition of a part of troubled Swiss Biber Holding AG.

It bought Biber's fine paper business Biberist which has annual net sales of around 1.5 billion markka for less than 300 million markka. Analysts said this was a fair price but many voiced concern at Metsa-Serla's acquisitiveness.
